data.narrative:
Lunar Energy, a Series D climate and energy company founded by Kunal Girotra, has raised over $300M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private companies and 1 public peer (LNZA) operating in the climate and energy sector at similar or adjacent funding stages.

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the $300M total raised as a proxy for current implied value and applies a 1.5x step-up multiplier typical for Series D advancement, yielding $450M. The peer-median approach examines four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Redwood Materials ($6.0B, Series D), KoBold Metals ($3.0B, Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B, Series C), and Amogy ($700M, Series C)—producing a median valuation of $2.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $6.0B.

Triangulating these methods yields a valuation range of $382M to $2.3B, with a median of $1.2B. The wide dispersion reflects material heterogeneity within the peer set; Redwood Materials at the high end likely reflects substantially de-risked technology or commercial traction relative to earlier-stage players. Key uncertainties include Lunar Energy's relative progress on technology maturation, capital intensity to commercial deployment, and addressable market capture relative to peers. The peer-median approach carries particular weight given the sector-aligned sample, though the stage-progression method provides a conservative floor anchored to actual capital deployed.
